title: Access Orchestration Patterns & Policy Templates (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
summary: A pragmatic playbook that maps RBAC v2 roles to environment-specific controls, provides compact policy templates, and documents the audit / SIEM export fields and evidence automation flows used to generate compliance artifacts for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures recommended access-orchestration patterns and concrete policy templates for Redwood’s three deployment surfaces (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). It complements the role matrix artifacts by focusing on how roles are applied, how to export audit telemetry for SIEMs, and how to automate evidence capture for audits and customer attestations.

Audience and scope:
- Primary audience: security engineers, platform engineers, solutions engineering, and compliance reviewers.
- Scope: RBAC v2 role application, least-privilege policy snippets (IAM/KMS/network), audit log schema and SIEM export best practices, evidence automation runbook for quarterly reviews. Does NOT replace team-specific onboarding checklists.

High-level design principles:
1) Single source of truth for role definitions (role catalog + canonical IDs).
2) Environment-specific enforcement: same logical roles, different bindings and supporting controls per environment.
3) Telemetry-first: every cross-boundary action must emit an audit event with a stable schema.
4) Evidence as code: policy snapshots, binding diffs and signed artifacts are generated automatically on schedule and on change.

Canonical RBAC v2 roles (logical names and intent):
- org_admin: full org-level administrative actions (billing, org-wide configs).
- security_auditor: read-only access to audit logs, export, policy snapshots, and compliance views.
- project_owner: manages projects, model registries, and rollout policies within a customer/project boundary.
- model_deployer: deploys model artifacts to inference endpoints/pools (cannot change org billing or higher-level network).
- inference_operator: manages runtime level (scaling, instance restarts) and sees live trace telemetry for incidents.
- dedicated_node_admin: manages dedicated GPU pools, node-level config, maintenance windows (dedicated only).
- private_network_admin: manages VPC connectors, peering, routing rules (private only).
- kms_operator: grant encryption key usage to workloads and rotate keys (restricted in hosted).
- billing_reader: read-only usage and cost reports.

Environment-specific mappings and controls:
1) Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood control plane):
   - Bindings: customers get project_owner / model_deployer at project scope. org_admin is internal only.
   - Additional controls: data-exfil prevention via outbound network restrictions, strict KMS proxying (hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS with customer-wrapped keys where required), and sanitized audit exports (no raw customer payloads).
   - SIEM exports: canonical event set but with payload hashes and redaction flags; include a customer-consented raw export pipeline for approved SOC processes.

2) Dedicated (customer-reserved capacity managed by Redwood):
   - Bindings: customer RPs can appoint dedicated_node_admins. Project_owner remains per project.
   - Additional controls: dedicated compute hosts are in a segregated pool; node-level access requires just-in-time access recorded by SRE.
   - KMS: mix of Redwood-managed and customer-supplied keys (KMSpolicy must allow Redwood service principal to decrypt).

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Bindings: customer-managed control plane or customer-integrated control plane. Redwood staff access is through formally approved bastion/JIT workflows.
   - Network: private network admin has full routing control; enforce least-privilege: do not grant private_network_admin general admin privileges over control-plane metadata.
   - KMS/HSM: customer-managed; policy templates below assume HSM-backed key referrals.

Audit log schema (required fields for every emitted event):
- event_time (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (stable UUID)
- service (string): e.g., inference.runtime, console.api, kms.service
- environment (string): hosted | dedicated | private
- cluster_id (string) or dedicated_pool_id
- actor_id (string): internal user id or service principal
- actor_roles (list of strings)
- actor_ip (string)
- action (string): e.g., model.deploy, model.infer, key.decrypt, iam.bind
- target_resource (string): resource canonical name (model:project/model_id, key:projects/.../keys/KEYID)
- request_id (string) correlates across services
- request_path (string) API path or route
- request_payload_hash (sha256) (string) - payload stored separately if allowed
- response_status (int) HTTP-like status code
- latency_ms (int)
- tokens_in (int) optional for inference calls
- tokens_out (int) optional for inference calls
- cost_estimate_tokens (float) optional
- decision_routing (string): which runtime variant served request (e.g., rtx-1/quant-8)
- fallback_reason (string) nullable: why a fallback was used
- cache_hit (boolean)
- pii_redaction_applied (boolean)
- signature (string) - signed digest of event (hosted and dedicated)

SIEM export best practices and mapping notes:
- Export formats supported: newline-delimited JSON over secure Kafka topic (preferred), syslog-over-TLS (legacy), and S3-drop for batch exports.
- Field mapping: SIEM prefers flattened fields. Map event_time->@timestamp, event_id->id, actor_id->user.id, actor_roles->user.roles, target_resource->object.name, request_payload_hash->object.content_hash, response_status->event.outcome.
- Redaction rules: do not export raw user prompts for hosted unless customer explicitly opts in. Instead export request_payload_hash and pii_redaction_applied flag.
- Enrichment: attach geoip and ASN enrichment at the SIEM ingestion layer; keep raw event as signed payload for re-ingestion.

Evidence automation runbook (how to generate compliance artifacts automatically):
1) Policy snapshot job (daily):
   - Export current IAM bindings and role definitions to S3 in JSONL and sign artifact with a rotation key.
   - Persist a diff against the previous snapshot; publish a change ticket if non-trivial role binding changes occur.
2) Audit export archive (rolling 90d hot, 365d cold):
   - Push NDJSON audit events to customer-specific S3 prefix or to customer SIEM endpoint.
   - Maintain manifest with SHA256 checksums and GPG signature for each daily archive.
3) Evidence bundle for customer audits (on-demand):
   - Bundle: latest policy snapshot, 90-day audit digest (signed), list of active service principals, JIT access logs, key-rotation records.
   - Create a short human summary that maps artifacts to control IDs (e.g., CIS/ISO/PCI controls mapping).
4) Retention and access controls:
   - Evidence bundles retained 3 years (configurable), access gated by security_auditor role and signed attestation.

Onboarding checklist for a new customer environment (minimal):
- Confirm environment type (hosted/dedicated/private) and KMS model.
- Map customer personnel to logical RBAC roles; prefer groups over individuals.
- Deploy policy snapshot job and verify manifest signatures.
- Configure SIEM export endpoint and validate exports with sample events.
- Run evidence bundle generation and verify artifacts and mappings.

Sample policy templates (drop-in, edit scope/principal as needed):
1) Minimal inference invocation policy (stringified JSON policy for reference):
{
  "Version": "2024-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["inference:InvokeModel"],
      "Resource": ["arn:redwood:model:{{project}}:{{model_id}}"],
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"redwood:Environment": "{{environment}}"}}
    }
  ]
}

2) KMS usage policy (for dedicated/private where customer supplies key):
{
  "Version": "2024-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"Service": ["redwood-inference.service"]},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:CallerEnvironment": "{{environment}}"}}
    }
  ]
}

3) Dedicated node admin minimal policy (RBAC style):
- Allowed: node.reboot, node.drain, node.patch, node.read
- Denied: any access to customer data stores and IAM binding changes

Operational recommendations and caveats:
- Prefer group-based bindings (SCIM/IdP groups) rather than per-user bindings for RBAC scalability.
- For hosted: do not allow raw prompt content to be stored unencrypted in long-term archives without explicit customer consent and documented controls.
- For private: require N-day key rotation proof and HSM attestation evidence on onboarding.
- All cross-boundary admin access must go through JIT workflow with automated attest logs retained in evidence bundles.

Open questions / future work items (tracking):
- Define stable control IDs that map to external frameworks (SOC2/ISO) for automation artifacts.
- Automate payload redaction verification in nightly compliance checks.
- Add synthetic event replay tests for SIEM pipelines to verify enrichment and parsers.

If you review this doc: please check the sample policy JSON for environment placeholders and the audit field list for any missing telemetry required by your SIEM. Comments inline are fine; we will iterate before finalizing templates for the policy repo.
recommendations: 1) Adopt the canonical event schema as the minimum for any service that crosses a trust boundary. 2) Start with group-based roles and maintain automated snapshots. 3) Validate SIEM mapping with two-week replay tests before relying on exports for alerting.
